inputs.text: Cyprus is moving toward a surveillance law that would weaken judicial oversight, one of the few checks on unchecked state power. Lawyers are warning about the amended bill ahead of a House vote on Thursday, and the stakes go well beyond legal procedure: people with the least power are often most exposed when surveillance operates without independent scrutiny. Privacy and civil liberties cannot depend on institutions policing themselves. The public needs transparency and strong safeguards before this change is approved.
